speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand your bleeding history, could you tell me how long the bleeding lasted after your wisdom tooth extraction and if you have noticed easy bruising elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience joint swelling or bleeding into the joints, and has this bleeding disorder affected other male relatives on your mother's side? I also need to know if you have ever had prolonged bleeding after other surgeries or dental work.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling and male relatives being affected, I suspect a coagulation factor deficiency. REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Factor VIII, Factor IX

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time (PT): 15 sec, Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT): 60 sec, Factor VIII: Not measured, Factor IX: Not measured

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT with a normal PT strongly suggests a deficiency in the intrinsic pathway, likely Factor VIII or IX. I need to distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, so REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII activity, Factor IX activity, and Von Willebrand Factor antigen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the factor assays were reported as normal despite a prolonged PTT, I suspect a lab artifact or a rare inhibitor like factor XI deficiency. To rule out a mixing error and check for inhibitors, I will order a mixing study and a Factor XI level. REQUEST TEST: PTT Mixing Study, Factor XI activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PTT Mixing Study: PTT corrects to normal (32 sec) after mixing with normal plasma, Factor XI activity: 25%

speaker: Doctor
text: The correction of the PTT in the mixing study confirms a factor deficiency rather than an inhibitor, and the reduced Factor XI activity points to Factor XI deficiency. Given your symptoms and test results, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Factor XI deficiency (Hemophilia C)
